clue.text: Pupil at Eton, possibly, without a bed?

indicators.note: without tells us to drop the letter named by the word that follows from the pupil

parts.note: Eton is a boarding school, so its pupils are typically boarders

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether an Eton schoolboy has been left with nowhere to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' reads as a mattress but means a flower bed, the sense of a garden strip along a lawn's edge. Eton is a famous English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden bed running along the edge of a lawn or path is called by this name.

clue.text: Most inspired lines about return of fine animal treatise

indicators.note: about means the first pieces go around the turned piece

parts.note: the most inspired is the best
RY, railway, is the usual crossword abbreviation for lines

indicators.note: return of asks for the word for fine to be read backwards

parts.note: A1 (written AI) means first-rate, fine

explanation.surface: A reviewer praises the finest passages around a reissue of a good book about beasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return of' turns the fine piece around and 'about' sets it inside: A1, written with an I, is old slang for first-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval bestiary is a descriptive treatise on real and fabulous creatures, often moralised.

clue.text: Sort of missile originally launched at country farmstead?

indicators.note: originally picks the opening letter of the word launched

parts.note: at and on both express position, as in at or on the coast
a grange is a country house with its farm buildings

explanation.surface: A rocket apparently fired from a rural farm.
explanation.definitionFit: Missiles are classed by reach, and one that can strike distant targets is so described.

clue.text: Part of piece using Berlin trombone section

indicators.note: a section is a slice taken out of the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: An orchestral passage showcases the trombones of a Berlin orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: The opening passage of a musical piece is its introduction, informally shortened.

clue.text: Illustrative of first proposal former politician put about

indicators.note: put about means placed around, so the politician's letters surround the proposal

parts.note: EX means former and a TORY is a British Conservative politician
the first plan put forward is plan A

explanation.surface: A one-time MP circulates an opening suggestion meant to clarify matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something illustrative serves to explain or make clear, which is what explanatory material does.

clue.text: Be compelled to abandon daughter born

indicators.note: abandon tells us the daughter is left out of the word for compulsion

parts.note: to need to do something is to be compelled to

explanation.surface: Someone is forced to give up their newborn daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Placed before a married woman's maiden name, this French word means born.

clue.text: Application concerning expedition

parts.note: RE means concerning, as in a letter's subject line
a quest is a journey or expedition in search of something

explanation.surface: A funding application relating to a planned exploration trip.
explanation.definitionFit: An application is a formal asking for something, the same as a petition or plea.

clue.text: City character consuming large cake

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing, so the first letters enclose the abbreviation

parts.note: EC is the postcode area for the City of London
an air is a manner or character, as in an air of mystery
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A city type is eating a big cake.
explanation.definitionFit: This choux pastry filled with cream and topped with chocolate is a small cake.

clue.text: Out to get to grips with old concept

indicators.note: to get to grips with suggests clasping, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: out means not in

explanation.surface: Someone is out to tackle an outdated idea.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion is an idea or concept held in the mind.

clue.text: A bar, one in city state

indicators.note: in tells us the bar and the one sit inside the city

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
to bar is to ban
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A pub, perhaps a single one, in an urban state.
explanation.definitionFit: Albania is a sovereign country, a state in the Balkans.

clue.text: Nothing that will shorten a long river

indicators.note: will shorten means the river's name loses its final letter

parts.note: the Nile is the world's longest river

explanation.surface: Asks what could possibly make a great river shorter.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites a geographic riddle; the answer is the river's name docked by one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Nil is the word for zero or nothing, especially in sports scores.

clue.text: Echo part of speech: king always worried about it

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

indicators.note: about it says the other pieces go round the part of speech

parts.note: e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, always
a verb is a part of speech
ate means worried, as in what's eating you

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson in which a king always frets about the echo of a word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about it' splits the poetic always open around the part of speech, with the king before and worried after.
explanation.definitionFit: To reverberate is to resound or re-echo, so it can stand for echo as a verb.

clue.text: Tendency of husband with something on the side?

parts.note: a bit on the side is a secret lover, so something on the side is a bit

explanation.surface: Asks whether a husband is prone to keeping a lover on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit on the side' is British slang for an extramarital affair.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit is a settled tendency or practice.

clue.text: Sea monster rocking the naval institute at first

indicators.note: rocking suggests shaking things up, so the letters are rearranged
at first picks the opening letter of institute

explanation.surface: A sea monster is shaking up the naval college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocking' shakes THE, NAVAL and I into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: The Leviathan is a Biblical sea creature, a name for any huge sea monster.

clue.text: Cancel comic sketch about hospital

indicators.note: about means the comic and sketch go around the hospital

parts.note: a wit is a joker or comic
to draw is to sketch
H is the map symbol for hospital

explanation.surface: A comedy sketch set in a hospital gets cancelled.
explanation.definitionFit: To withdraw an offer or remark is to retract or cancel it.

clue.text: Rodent catcher, one regularly consulting army doctor?

parts.note: MO is a Medical Officer, an army doctor
a user is one who consults or uses something regularly

explanation.surface: Asks whether a patient who keeps seeing the army doctor is a ratcatcher.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat good at catching mice and rats is called this.

clue.text: Politician raised mistake by hosts — fruitful outcome

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word is read upwards, that is backwards

parts.note: a Lib is a Liberal politician

indicators.note: hosts means holds inside, so the word by surrounds the error

parts.note: taken as written
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: A politician hoisted by an error that hosts a productive result.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'raised' reads the Liberal upwards, and 'hosts' has the small word swallow the mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A bilberry is the blue fruit of a moorland shrub, playfully a fruitful outcome.

clue.text: Approach — thus to get to old rail union?

parts.note: NUR was the National Union of Railwaymen, now defunct; the word for sprint written upwards in a down entry spells its initials

explanation.surface: Asks how one arrives at a defunct railway union.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction in a down entry: write the word for dash going upwards and you get the initials of the National Union of Railwaymen.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-up is the approach a bowler or jumper makes before the action.

clue.text: Organ primarily employed at recitals

indicators.note: primarily picks the opening letter of each of the next words

explanation.surface: An organ is chiefly played at recitals.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a church organ; the definition is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: The ear is the sense organ of hearing.

clue.text: Ninth character sounds angry, seeing ugly building

indicators.note: sounds tells us to take the pronunciation of the letter, spelt as a word

parts.note: I is the ninth letter of the alphabet
sore means angry, especially in American usage

explanation.surface: A letter of the alphabet seems annoyed on spotting an unsightly structure.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyesore is something very unpleasant to look at, such as a hideous building.

clue.text: Billy's alert, surprisingly, grudgingly being one

indicators.note: surprisingly signals that the letters are reordered unexpectedly

parts.note: the name with its S counted as a letter

explanation.surface: Billy is alert, unexpectedly, though reluctantly so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' reorders BILLYS and ALERT. 'grudgingly' has three syllables, so it is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A word with three syllables is so called, and grudg-ing-ly is an example.

clue.text: Army command pushy types seek ?

explanation.surface: An army order is also what forward people crave.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers come to attention on command, and show-offs crave notice.

clue.text: The old prognostication for small farmers once

parts.note: ye is an archaic spelling of the
an omen is a sign foretelling the future

explanation.surface: An ancient prophecy for smallholders of the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeomen were historically freeholders cultivating their own modest landholdings.

clue.text: Tot three-quarters of foot-soldiers demanded

indicators.note: three-quarters of keeps six of the eight letters, dropping the last two

parts.note: infantry are soldiers who fight on foot

explanation.surface: A young child insists on being included among the troops.
explanation.definitionFit: An infant is a baby or very young child, a tot.

clue.text: Nursed by girl and boy, fighting men got better

indicators.note: nursed by means held within, so the soldiers go inside the girl's name

parts.note: Amelia is a girl's name
OR is other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
Ted is a boy's name

explanation.surface: Soldiers tended by a young woman and a lad recovered.
explanation.definitionFit: To ameliorate is to improve, so the past tense means improved or got better.

clue.text: Medley of popular tunes — quite bold arrangement

indicators.note: an arrangement of music fits the surface, and here the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A medley of hits presented as a rather daring musical arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A quodlibet is a musical piece combining several familiar tunes, a medley.

clue.text: Jack accommodates French writer, being a publican once

indicators.note: accommodates means houses inside, so the sailor contains the writer

parts.note: jack tar, or tar, is a sailor
Jules Verne was a French novelist

explanation.surface: A sailor puts up a French author while working as a pub landlord.
explanation.definitionFit: A taverner was historically the keeper of a tavern, an innkeeper.

clue.text: Literary effort a woman read after thirty days

indicators.note: read after says the woman comes after the month in the reading

parts.note: November has thirty days, abbreviated NOV
Ella is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman reads a book after a month.
explanation.definitionFit: A novella is a short novel, a piece of fiction longer than a short story.

clue.text: Show up Republicans in area — this writer's

parts.note: R is Republican, doubled for the plural
this writer's means I have, contracted to I've

explanation.surface: The author notes Republicans have turned up in the district.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrive at a place is to turn up or show up there.

clue.text: Wife keeping up a city house in haphazard manner

indicators.note: keeping up in a down entry means the wife sits below, holding the rest above

parts.note: NY is New York

explanation.surface: A wife maintains a city home in a slapdash way.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the last letter supports those above it, so 'keeping up' puts W at the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Done anyhow means done carelessly or in a haphazard way.

clue.text: Mountain note, soldiers climb

indicators.note: climb in a down entry means the letters run upwards, that is backwards

parts.note: soh is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale
TA is the Territorial Army, British reserve soldiers

explanation.surface: Soldiers noted climbing a peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climb' turns SOHTA upward to give the mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Athos is a Greek mountain famous for its monasteries.

clue.text: Trouble initially described in a circular letter

indicators.note: in places the initial letter between the other two pieces

parts.note: O is the round letter of the alphabet

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of described

explanation.surface: Problems initially described in a round-robin letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ado means fuss or bother, trouble, as in much ado about nothing.
